messages:
sara_sales: Hey team -- BankCo POC kickoff tomorrow. They want Redwood Private (on-prem appliance) but need initial data seeding via AWS Snowball Edge. Asking: connectivity model (PrivateLink vs peering), exact firewall/IPs for the POC, and any pricing impact for Snowball + 30d POC reserved nodes.

pedro_networks: High-level: two options we usually propose:
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints) into their VPC -> easiest cross-account isolation, no peering setup. Uses TCP 443 to our ENIs.
- VPC Peering (or TGW peering) -> preserves original client src IPs, lower hop count, but requires route/peering approvals and potentially cross-account route maintenance.
Which does BankCo prefer on their side? If they're highly locked down, PrivateLink tends to be lower friction.

anya_se: Firewall snippet for PrivateLink POC (customer to allow outbound):
```
# Allow outbound to Redwood interface endpoints (HTTPS)
- ALLOW tcp 443 to redwood-privatelink-eips (we'll provide exact /32 list)
# Control plane (console/updates)
- ALLOW tcp 443 to redwood-controlplane.*.amazonaws.com
# Snowball -> initial data transfer (from on-prem to Snowball)
- ALLOW tcp 22 to snowball appliance local IPs during transfer window
# Management access (SRE) - limited / jumpbox
- ALLOW tcp 22 from our ops IPs (one-off)
```
Note: we'll provide a signed IP allowlist for the POC week. For VPC peering the main ask is route table entries and SG rules to permit the same ports but source IPs will be preserved.

kate_security: A couple security points for Snowball + Private deploy:
- Snowball Edge requires final manifest uploads and communicates with AWS endpoints; customer must allow egress to S3 control endpoints (443) during job.
- Chain-of-custody: BankCo asked for physical custody docs. We can supply our standard data handling addendum + contact at AWS for Snowball handling.
- KMS: For on-prem private deploy we support customer-managed CMKs. We'll need the KMS ARN ahead of time.

jake_finance: Pricing notes for sales
- Snowball: customer pays AWS Snowball job fee (we can estimate ~USD 300-500 for one Edge device, depends on region/size).
- POC: 30d POC license for Private is discounted (confirm 50% off list) + setup fee for on-prem appliance.
- Dedicated vs Private pricing delta: dedicated cloud reserved capacity is usage-based monthly commit; private is license+support. I'll draft a quote once we know whether they need sustained capacity after seed.

pedro_networks: Two technical caveats to call out for the presales doc:
1) Source IP preservation: if BankCo needs original client IP on logs, choose VPC peering or a NAT-preserving proxy. PrivateLink -> NLBs will NAT flows so you see provider IPs.
2) TLS inspect/firewall: if they do TLS inspection, ensure the Snowball transfer and our management traffic are excluded or provide certs so inspection doesn't break manifest uploads.

sara_sales: Good call. BankCo security team flagged TLS inspect concerns and requires preserved client IP in app logs for fraud detection. They prefer VPC peering but their netops hates peering approvals.

anya_se: If they insist on preserved IP + minimal ops approvals, propose TGW+route table entries with a short-run peering request template we provide (one-page netops checklist). We can also offer a short-living peering (delete after POC) to reduce long-term approvals.

kate_security: I'll attach our KMS integration checklist and the Snowball chain-of-custody template to the ticket. Also suggest including an explicit IP allowlist SLA for the POC window.

deploy-bot: :calendar: Scheduled: POC infra readiness call with BankCo on Tue 10:00am PST. Invite sent to all participants.

sara_sales: Next steps for handoff ->
- Pedro: prepare two connectivity diagrams (PrivateLink + VPC peering) with exact route/SG changes and quick netops checklist.
- Anya: generate provisional firewall allowlist (CIDRs) for the POC and Snowball windows.
- Kate: share KMS + Snowball ATO paperwork.
- Jake: estimate Snowball+30d POC line items for the quote.
I'll follow up with BankCo to pick one model after the readiness call. :thumbsup:
